name: System Wake Lock
plain: A way to keep the CPU awake while the screen is off; never shipped.
meaning: The spec once listed a system lock that would keep the machine awake with the screen off. No browser shipped it because of battery abuse risk. Proxies are audio playback, background sync and push.

limits.headline: Can't keep your device awake with the screen off; no browser ever shipped this
can: Use workarounds such as audio playing, push or background sync instead
Keep the screen on while the page is visible, which is a different feature
cannot: Keep the computer awake with the screen off from a web page
Run long downloads this way, since it was dropped for battery abuse risk

story.what_it_is: A way to keep the whole device awake with the screen off. It was never released.
story.for_you: You cannot do this on the web. A site cannot keep your device awake after the screen goes off. This protects your battery. Only the screen lock exists.
story.for_makers: Makers wanted long background tasks such as downloads, uploads and music. Browser makers declined to ship it for battery reasons. Developers use push, background fetch and media sessions instead.

use_cases.example: A web music player wanted to keep playing through a long sleep. It uses media playback instead, which the system treats as allowed.
A web backup tool wanted to upload photos overnight with the screen off. It uses background sync and upload retries instead.
A browser game wanted to run a simulation while the device sleeps. It uses push alerts and saved state instead.
A web run tracker wanted to keep recording a route with the screen off. It needs an installed app for that.
A web video downloader wanted to keep downloading overnight. It uses background fetch instead.
A web sleep or health logger wanted to stay awake to record data. It cannot do so on the web.
A web kiosk wanted to keep running during idle. It uses the screen wake lock instead.

history.change: System lock removed from the spec and not implemented
